summary: Edwin M. Lee Apartments, an affordable multifamily building at 1150 Third Street on Mission Bay South Block 3 East: a five-story building with offices, a garage and a community room, sponsored by the Chinatown Community Development Center with Swords to Plowshares. The city permit was filed in December 2016 and marked complete on June 17, 2020; the Examiner reported that it had housed residents since February (2021) and that the grand opening was held in May 2021. Sources give 119 total units and 118 affordable units; the 62 veterans' and 56 or 57 family units are counted differently (see the unit-count note).

facts.value: 8711 / 026 (per the DataSF permit records); Venue, 1155 4th St, is on the same block, lot 025
Chinatown Community Development Center with Swords to Plowshares (project sponsor per OCII fiscal year 2015-16 report)
Leddy Maytum Stacy Architects (with Saida + Sullivan Design Partners), per SF YIMBY; OCII's report spells the firm "Stacey"

119 total units and 118 affordable units per OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report ('Total Units 119', 'Total Affordable Units 118'); the permit describes '119 dwelling' units; the Examiner (May 2021) and the Chinatown Community Development Center page say 118 ('62 units designated for formerly homeless veterans and 56 units for low-income families'). Swords to Plowshares lists 62 veterans and 57 low-income families. No source read says what the one unit between 118 and 119 is.
$78 million from federal, state and city sources, per SF YIMBY (a news report)

DataSF's official address point for 1150 3rd St (address ID 741013) is recorded on parcel 8711026, and this record's outline is that parcel (Assessor lots 8711026A and 8711026B). Until 2026-10-12 the outline was an idealized rectangle that the parcel overlapped by 93% and that covered 99% of the parcel (Pier & Point's own calculation in a local metric projection).

open_questions: Does the outline match the building's real footprint? The outline is now the parcel the address point sits on, which can include yard or plaza around the building; no source read gives the building's own footprint.

Unit count: OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report lists 119 total units and 118 affordable units, and the permit and Swords to Plowshares give 119; the Examiner and the Chinatown Community Development Center page say 118 (62 veteran plus 56 family units); SF YIMBY gives 118; SFBay (2018) says 'a total of 119 affordable units, 62 for homeless veterans, and 56 for low-income families', which sums to 118; Swords to Plowshares says 62 veterans and 57 families (119). Which family-unit count (56 or 57) is right, and what the one unit between 118 affordable and 119 total is (the source reports do not say; it may be a manager's unit), is not established.
Square footage differs: SF YIMBY gives 123,700 and the Chinatown Community Development Center page gives 81,295; not reconciled, so neither is recorded as a fact.

The exact move-in date is not stated: the Examiner (May 2021) says residents since 'February' without naming the year, and the permit shows completion in June 2020. The 2020-06-17 milestone is the permit's own completion date, not an occupancy date.
No OCII Commission document or press release for the opening was read as text; the primary-source figures come from OCII's fiscal year 2015-16 report and the city permit data.
Final construction cost was not found; the $73,040,010 is a 2016 projection and the $45,000,000 is the permit's own estimate.
